item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 27: Members of the Tampa Bay Rays celebrate after Ben Williamson #15 of the Tampa Bay Rays hits a walk off single in the 12th inning to defeat the Milwaukee Brewers during Game Four of the 2026 World Series presented by Capital One at Tropicana Field on Tuesday, October 27, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images In 2011, Dan Shaughnessy famously counted the Rays out when they were down 7-0 to New York in Game 162 while the Boston/Baltimore game was in a rain delay. Shortly thereafter, the magic happened propelling the Rays into the postseason. It took 12 innings and 4 hours and 15 minutes of baseball for the magic to happen as the Rays avoided being swept with a 4-3 comeback win. Griffin Jax got the Rays through four innings, but the lift was a lot harder than the line score looked. Jax had nine batted ball events with exit velocity of at least 96 MPH and expected batting averages of at least .770, but early on, only an opposite field line drive single by Jackson Chourio with one out in the 3rd inning safely found the synthetic surface. That changed in the 4th when a two-out single by Sal Frelich, which was 104.4 off the bat, was quickly followed by a 98.9 MPH double by Cooper Pratt to tie up the game. The Brewers put nine balls in play off Jax and only a Brice Turang groundout had an exit velocity below 96.0 MPH. Their offense, overall, made outstanding contact despite the low-scoring affair: By the bottom of the 4th, the Rays did something they could not do in Game 3, and that was plate a second run. It was more a bad process-good outcome type of play though as Junior Caminero should not have been moving on contact to the left side from second base, yet somehow avoided the tag and being called out the baseline to score on an errant throw by David Hamilton to get a hustling DeLuca. DeLuca would be eliminated on a fielder’s choice groundout by Chandler Simpson, who himself would soon be eliminated after getting picked off by JoJo Romero. That 2-1 lead lasted all of three pitches when Jax’s final pitch of the evening came in at a game-low 93.4 MPH and Hamilton yanked that 0-2 pitch into the stands to tie the game and make up for his throwing error: View Link The pen was once again asked to get 15 outs, which has not gone well in previous events this series, this month, and this season. Kevin Kelly got the first three while stranding a two-out walk to Christian Yelich in front of William Contreras. Jax’s outing overall was effective by the measures, but not the overall outcome. The PitcherList report card even says as much, and the results went from B+ to C+ with that last swing by Hamilton: Nick Martinez came in of relief for Kevin Kelly and had a similar path of stranding a two-out baserunner. Martinez would go on to work two innings in relief before handing it off to Bryan Baker in the 8th. A well-rested Baker looked sharp with his changeups

item.title: Rays win thriller to thwart Brewers in World Series
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays celebrate after Ben Williamson's single clinches a dramatic extra-inning win in the World Series (Carmen Mandato) The Tampa Bay Rays staged a dramatic extra-innings rally to keep their World Series dream alive on Tuesday, walking off a 4-3 victory against the Milwaukee Brewers to avoid a clean sweep. Tampa Bay's Ben Williamson singled a ground ball to right field in the bottom of the 12th inning to complete a thrilling comeback at Tropicana Field that ensures a game five on Wednesday. "Just shows the resiliency of this group," Williamson said afterwards. "We continue to fight and that's been the motto this series and this whole season." Milwaukee had looked to be heading for a 4-0 series triumph after rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt launched a solo home run in the 12th inning to give the Brewers a 3-2 lead on the night. But with their season on the line, the Rays flipped the script, igniting a fightback when a throwing error by Brewers' third baseman Joey Ortiz allowed Junior Caminero to reach first base. The Brewers brought in reliever Shane Drohan to replace Antonio Senzatela but the Rays continued to prosper with catcher Liam Hicks singling to send Caminero to third base with no outs. Jonny DeLuca then singled to drive in a run to make it 3-3, and shortly after that leveler Chandler Simpson singled to load the bases with no outs. Pinch hitter Williamson then came in and steered a ground ball to right field to score the winning run. rcw/amz

In extra innings, Cooper Pratt's solo home run appeared like it would be the signature moment of the World Series, giving the Brewers a 3-2 lead. However, Tampa Bay battled back with an inspired bottom of the 12th inning. The Rays took advantage of an error as each of their first five hitters reached base, allowing Tampa Bay to walk it off. The heroes were Johnny DeLuca, whose single tied the game, and Ben Williamson, whose pinch-hit single ended the game and extended the series. Both teams pitched extremely well, holding the opposing offense down throughout the game with their top arms. In the end, it was two Brewers errors that led to two Rays runs, one by David Hamilton and another by Joey Ortiz, which opened the door for Tampa Bay's struggling offense. No team in the World Series has ever forced a Game 6 after going down 3-0. The Brewers will send Jacob Misiorowski to the mound, hoping the expected Cy Young winner can end the series. item.title: Paul George credits ‘MVP’ Jayson Tatum for taking Celtics home vs. Nets
item.description: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images Paul George credits ‘MVP’ Jayson Tatum for taking Celtics home vs. Nets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It may have taken until the very last millisecond of overtime, but it counts as a win all the same for the Boston Celtics . The Celtics were pushed to the brink by the winless Brooklyn Nets, but Jayson Tatum put his foot down and decided that Boston wasn’t about to suffer a crushing loss at home — sending the Nets home heartbroken with a game-winning buzzer-beater to give the Cs a 125-124 victory. Everyone in TD Garden knew that the Celtics were going to find Tatum on that final possession. But Boston drew up an incredible play to get Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. switched onto Tatum, and Tatum swished home a jumper from right around the foul line to give Boston their third win of the season. It is the responsibility of the team’s best player to get the job done , and Paul George knows that Tatum is never the type to shy away from the responsibilities of an MVP-level player. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We got the ball to the MVP and he took us home,” George said in his postgame presser, via Justin Turpin of WEEI. “We got the ball to the MVP and he took us home.” Paul George speaks on the Jayson Tatum game-winner 🗣️ (via @JustinmTurpin ) pic.twitter.com/3GKOwVVW6p — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 28, 2026 Indeed, Tatum was on a heater on Tuesday, and it would have been a shame had the Celtics actually lost that game. Tatum finished the night with 40 points on 10-of-20 shooting from the field and 18-of-22 shooting from the charity stripe, a performance that’s befitting of an MVP-level player like him. If the Celtics lost, they wouldn’t have had anyone to blame but themselves anyway. They missed free throws in regulation that kept the door ajar for the Nets, which Brown then pried open with a game-tying triple to send the game to overtime. If it weren’t for some mental lapses from the Nets , the Celtics may have fallen to 2-2 on the season. But a win is a win, and there was no better way for them to squeak out a victory than by giving the ball to their superstar and letting him do his thing. The Rays won 4-3 on a walk-off single by Ben Williamson, cutting Milwaukee’s series lead to 3-1 and sending the World Series to Game 5. Milwaukee immediately threatened, putting runners on the corners in the top of the first thanks to two walks by Rays starter Griffin Jax and a throwing error by catcher Liam Hicks. Brice Turang had a chance to give the Brewers an early lead, but he grounded out to short to strand both runners. Tampa Bay couldn’t get anything going against Dustin May in the bottom half of the frame, as he capped off a 1-2-3 first by striking out Junior Caminero looking. The second inning went less smoothly. Hicks led off with a single, and Jonny DeLuca followed with a grounder to Turang at second that nearly became a double play, but the speedy DeLuca beat the relay to first. That brought up Chandler Simpson, who took a strike, fouled off a couple more pitches, then laced a double down the right-field line to score DeLuca from first. item.title: “This Is Exactly Why Cathy Engelbert Needs to Go”: WNBA World Reacts As Dream Issues Revealing Statement About Game 6 Venue Change Fiasco
item.description: Angel Reese © X/ @AtlantaDream The Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream have provided an entertaining WNBA Finals. The Valkyries lead the series 3-2 after Monday’s 64-55 win. They defeated Angel Reese and co. in back-to-back games to inch closer to the title. However, the discourse has slightly shifted from basketball. The venue for Game 6 was changed from the Dream’s Gateway Center Arena to the Atlanta Hawks’ State Farm Arena to accommodate 17,000 fans. Now, if the Valkyries are crowned champions in Game 6, the celebrations could be affected due to the Hawks’ game against the Cavaliers on the same day. The Dream released a statement on Tuesday regarding their plea to the WNBA about the scheduling of the WNBA Finals series. They raised concerns about the scheduling conflict; however, their concerns apparently did not receive attention from the league. Fans were fuming online after Atlanta addressed the Dream fans in the open letter. “This is exactly why (retiring WNBA Commissioner) Cathy (Engelbert) needs to go,” one fan said . Cathy Engelbert announced her retirement and will be leaving her position as the WNBA commissioner after December. However, fans are still blaming her for issues in the league. Atlanta Dream’s open letter to their fans In an open letter, the Dream management told fans that the franchise tried to avoid the inconvenience that would be caused by a Thursday afternoon game. However, the WNBA did not pay attention to those concerns, the team said. “Two months ago, when the WNBA finalized playoff dates and times, we raised concerns that the W Finals schedule conflicted with NBA games at State Farm Arena. As we moved through the playoffs, we reiterated those concerns. Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved,” part of the statement read . “Perhaps it was assumed that the Dream would not make it this far. Perhaps, our place in the Finals was not accounted for. Whatever the reason, the reality is that we are here. UConn’s Defense Destroys Purdue Getty Dan Hurley during an October 20th game between UConn and Michigan State. Offensively, the Boilermakers couldn’t get anything going in this one. The visitors went just two for 25 from three point range (.08%), struggling mightily from the perimeter in Hartford. From the field, Purdue only connected on 32.8% of its shot attempts. The Huskies got off to a fast start, leading 35-20 at halftime. Even more impressive, Dan Hurley’s guys did so despite star Braylon Mullins having a middling night offensively (nine points). Connecticut didn’t let up in the slightest, continuing to cushion its lead following the break. Freshman Colben Landrew led UConn with 15 points, followed closely by Jayden Ross with 13. Eight different members of the roster notched a bucket in this one, with 28 of the team’s points coming from the bench. The scary thing for opposing teams? There’s room for the Huskies to get even better, at least on offense. UConn only shot 28.6% from three-point range. Even modest improvement from long distance would go a long way for this title-contending crew. What’s Next for the Huskies? It’s been smooth sailing for UConn this preseason, having also earned wins over Syracuse and Michigan State. Now, the real work begins for Dan Hurley and company. UConn men’s basketball gets its schedule started on November 2nd, a home game against Gardner-Webb. Immediately after, the level of competition gets ramped up a notch. Following their showdown with the Wolverines, the Huskies will take on five more ranked opponents during non-conference play. That includes marquee matchups with #5 Arizona, #2 Duke, and #3 Illinois. After that, the always-interesting Big East slate gets underway right before the new year. If Tuesday’s game proves anything, this UConn group will be an extremely tough out for opponents. Unlike some of the nation’s other elite teams, the Huskies are capable of winning even if the shots aren’t falling. That’s without mentioning the experience littered across this roster, with several members of last season’s Final Four squad returning to Storrs. A win over Purdue isn’t quite as impressive compared to seasons past. After all, the Boilermakers come into the new season unranked, and it’s easy to see why. Still, taking down any Big Ten foe by 23 points deserves praise. The college basketball world has to be a bit worried seeing a Dan Hurley-coached team taking care of business in dominant fashion. item.title: Jayden Daniels Trade Pitch Nets Three 1st-Round Picks From Contender
item.description: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. Getty The Washington Commanders can’t be this dumb, right? History tells us they could be. That’s why a trade pitch for Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels from NFL Draft Bites’ Chad Forbes deserves serious consideration, and you should ask yourself one question: Which team says “No” first? “(Commanders) in tough predicament. Jayden Daniels due for a new contract in offseason,” Forbes wrote on his official X account on Tuesday. “Deal will be over $60M per season and potentially surpass Mahomes as the league’s highest-paid player. Played just 11 of last 23 games. Do you at least listen? Say the Vikings offer 2027-2028-2029 1st-rounders?” Toss in current Vikings starter Kyler Murray as a stopgap until the Commanders can draft another quarterback, and it starts to seem like a real proposition. Commanders fan and Pardon My Take co-host Eric “PFT Commenter” Sollenberger chimed in as the voice of reason. “The ‘tough predicament’ in this case is whether or not to trade the best QB your team has had in at least 35 years,” PFT wrote on his official X account in response to Forbes. “No offense to Taylor Heinicke.” Commanders on Brink of Another Lost Season We never get to this point if the Commanders don’t struggle like they have the last few years. Since going 12-5 and making it to the NFC Championship Game in Daniels’ bravura rookie season in 2024, the former No. 2 overall pick has missed more games than he’s played. That meant he missed 10 games in 2025 as Washington went 5-12, and 2 games already in 2026 as his team has stumbled to a 1-4-1 start. The Vikings are the NFL’s lone unbeaten team left standing at 6-0. Touch Decision Awaits on Daniels’ Contract Everyone can agree that giving Daniels a contract that makes him one of the NFL’s highest-paid players right now isn’t a no-brainer — and it’s OK to remind ourselves that he still has another full season left on the 4-year, $37.7 million rookie contract he signed in 2024. Daniels and his mom/agent can complain all they want this offseason — the fact is, the Commanders don’t have to pay him yet. Yes, the other two quarterbacks in the top three picks in his draft will get massive deals after this year — Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (No. 1 overall) and New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (No. 3 overall) — but they’ve proven their worth. Before the season, Spotrac’s Michael Ginnitti released a list of projected “Next Man Up” contracts at every NFL position — meaning the next contracts that will reset the market for each position. He included Williams and Maye, but not Daniels. “It’s not a predicament at all,” Anarchist Bub Carrington wrote on X . “Pay the man. He’s a star quarterback, and every metric shows it. Get him a real coach and an offensive line.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Jayden Daniels Trade Pitch Nets Three 1st-Round Picks From Contender appeared first on HEAVY .

item.description: If you’ve attended or watched a Cincinnati Bengals game, have you ever wondered how a player like DJ Turner decided he wanted to be a football player? And how he made it happen? Donyale Turner, mother of Bengals cornerback DJ Turner, is featured in episode two of The Enquirer’s special-edition podcast series “Beyond Sunday" spotlighting five moms of Bengals players. item.title: Kings drop final game of road trip to Blackhawks
item.description: Chicago Blackhawks center Frank Nazar (91) looks on at the puck during an NHL game against the Los Angeles Kings on December 6, 2025 in Los Angeles, Calif. CHICAGO -- The Los Angeles Kings surrendered an early lead and fell 2-1 to the Chicago Blackhawks at United Center on Tuesday, closing out their five-game road trip with a loss. For this being their second game of a back-to-back and final game of the road trip, the Kings started off very fast. The Kings struck first immediately after an opening-shift goal from the fourth line, as center Samuel Helenius knocked in a loose puck that was wrested on-net by Jared Wright. Wright's shot trickled between the legs of Blackhawks' goaltender Spencer Knight, and was subsequently knocked in after a stick battle in the crease. The goal marked Helenius' first point of the season. Andre Lee and Wright each picked up an assist on the goal. Chicago, working from a 1-0 deficit, pushed hard in the second period to find an equalizer. At the 14:26 mark of the second, Joel Armia was called for a tripping penalty on Blackhawks' center Anton Frondell. Kings' goaltender Anton Forsberg neutralized the Blackhawks' power play with a pair of nice saves late, however Armia drew an interference penalty as he received the puck while leaving the penalty box. The Kings, without their best penalty killer for four consecutive minutes, immediately allowed the tying goal 11 seconds into the second penalty to Roman Kantserov. Kantserov's goal at 16:40 in the second was his fifth of the season, assisted by Connor Bedard and Teuvo Teravainen. The Kings gained a huge advantage late in the second period after Armia drew a high-sticking double minor penalty against Blackhawks' defenseman Sam Rinzel. To kickoff the third period, the Kings had nearly three minutes of power play time - however they only mustered one shot on goal while in the advantage. "We've got to be better in that area out on the power play. We had one last game, I was hoping that it was going to build some confidence off of that," said Kings right winger Adrian Kempe. "We've got to be better. We've got to be better at communicating, passes - just everything." Unable to grasp any momentum, the Kings gave up a goal shortly after the failed power play, as Blackhawks' defenseman Wyatt Kaiser buried a wrist shot five-hole from the left face-off circle 7:17 into the period. "We've been here too many times in the third period, 1-1, with a chance to win a game and we don't get it done. It's on us. We've got to get that done," Kings coach Peter Laviolette said. "The record could be a lot different if we're closing out third periods." Kaiser's tiebreaker ended up being the difference, as Knight was nails to close the game - stopping the Kings' final three shots on goal and 25-of-26 on the night. Forsberg, despite earning the loss, stopped 25-of-27 shots and singlehandedly kept the Kings in the game in the final two periods as the Blackhawks' offensive barrage rained down on him.

He was acquired on Friday and was ready to go by the time Tuesday rolled around, kicking off the Devils road trip with a start against the Dallas Stars. His performance wasn’t special. He saved 16 of the 17 shots he faced as the Devils offense steamrolled the Stars in a 5-1 win. Hellebuyck wasn’t asked to do much and didn’t stand out because of it. He didn't win the game but didn't lose it either. The recent game, however, wasn’t about him, even with all the eyes on him before the puck drop. Hellebuyck, who has spent a lot of time in the spotlight, was nowhere near it on Tuesday night. It’s because the team in front of him stole the show, with a dominant performance that extended the Devils' winning streak to four games. Devils Limited The Shots On The Net A theme for the Devils is limiting shots regardless of who is in the net. Whether it was Jake Allen, Nico Daws, or Hellebuyck in the latest game, the defense has limited shots and dared teams to shoot from tough angles. The Devils Hope Their Core Can Go Up Against Any In The NHL With games against the Dallas Stars, Colorado Avalanche, and Vegas Golden Knights this week, the Devils will find out how good their top-end talent and roster altogether are. It wasn’t that way to start the season, as the defense not only struggled but also allowed teams to find easy goals in the net front. Now that the defense has bought in and is coming into form, they are protecting their goaltenders and blanking offenses. The 5-1 win against the Stars was the third game in a row that the Devils held a team to one goal, and in the last five games, they've only allowed 11 goals. Hellebuyck needed an easy game, and the Devils gave it to him. He wasn’t asked to save the day, and for a goaltender who hasn’t faced NHL action since April, it was a good way to get back into it.
